questions.question: How is National Income calculated?

options.text: Net National Product - indirect taxes + subsidy
Net Domestic Product – Indirect Taxes – Depreciation
Net Domestic Product + Indirect Taxes – Depreciation
Net National Product + indirect taxes - subsidy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Net National Product - indirect taxes + subsidy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

There are 3 methods to calculate National Income

 
• Income Method
 
• Expenditure Method
 
• Product Method

According to the product method,

National income or NNPFC = GDPMP - Consumption of fixed capital + NFIA - Net Indirect Taxes

NNPFC = Net National Product - Indirect Taxes + Subsidy

questions.question: Economic activities, though, are grouped together into three different categories are highly _____ .
questions.solution:
3 different categories in which economic activities are categories,

 
 

 
 
**Categories**

 
 
 
**Features**

 
 
 

 
 
Primary sector

 
 
 
It includes activities like farming, oil extraction etc, which provides Raw Material to the secondary sector.

 
 
 

 
 
Secondary sector

 
 
 
It includes factories and mills which work upon the Raw Material provided by Primary sector and convert them into the finished product.

 
 
 

 
 
Tertiary sector

 
 
 
The Tertiary sector includes retailing activities which deliver the finished product, produced in the secondary sector to the desired customer.

 
 
 

 

All the three sectors are highly interdependent since work of each sector is important for the proper functioning of other two sector

questions.question:
Which among the following is/are Organ/organs of the Indian government?

I. The media

II. The legislature

III. The Executive

IV. The judiciary
questions.solution:
In accordance with the doctrine of separation of powers, the government is divided into three organs:

 
 

 
 
**Organs**

 
 
 
**Features**

 
 
 

 
 
The Executive

 
 
 
The executive is the organ exercising authority in and holding responsibility for the governance of a state

 
 
 

 
 
The Legislative

 
 
 
A legislature is a deliberative assembly with the authority to make laws for a political entity.

 
 
 

 
 
The Judiciary

 
 
 
The judiciary is the system of courts that interprets and applies the law in the name of the state.

questions.question: The part of food that is NOT digested in the body is ______ ?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The major component in the rigid cell walls in plants is cellulose.
 
• The structure of cellulose consists of long polymer chains of glucose units connected by a beta acetal linkage.
 
• The acetal linkage is beta which makes it different from starch. This peculiar difference in acetal linkages results in a major difference in digestibility in humans.
 
• Humans are unable to digest** cellulose **__because the appropriate enzymes to break down the beta acetal linkages are lacking in the human body.

questions.question: Which of the following processes keeps plants cool?
questions.solution: Plants cool themselves by performing Transpiration process. When the surrounding atmosphere heats up, plants will often release excess water into the air from their leaves. By releasing evaporated water, plants cool themselves and the surrounding environment.

questions.question: In which organ blood is stored?
questions.solution:
__Concept__-

__
 
• The spleen is the largest lymphatic organ of the body.
 
• Lymphatic organs are the ones that carry the clear fluid lymph in them.
 
• The spleen synthesizes antibodies in its white pulp and removes antibody-coated bacteria.
 
• Spleen is an organ on the left side of the abdomen below the stomach.
 
• It is also known as the “graveyard of blood” as it filters the blood by removing microbes and worn-out RBCs.
 
• Spleen also has a large reservoir of erythrocytes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec7a08c62904a915ee5d8d2fdf97c43209b89dc7b4d52a69350b18a67998c2d6.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The spleen plays important roles in regard to red blood cells and the immune system. 
 
• It removes old red blood cells, creates new blood cells and holds a reserve of blood.

questions.question: The meter that measures the distance moved by the vehicle is called _________ ?
questions.solution:
** Meters**

 
 
 
** Functions**

 
 
 

 
 
Speedometer

 
 
 
A speedometer or a speed meter is a gauge that measures and displays the instantaneous speed of a vehicle.

 
 
 

 
 
Odometer

 
 
 
An odometer or odograph is an instrument used for measuring the distance traveled by a vehicle, such as a bicycle or a car. 

 
 
 

 
 
Chronometer

 
 
 
A chronometer is a specific type of mechanical timepiece tested and certified to meet certain precision standards.

 
 
 

 
 
Barometer

 
 
 
A barometer is a scientific instrument used in meteorology to measure atmospheric pressure.

 
 
 

 

**Note:** __Speedometer is used to measure the velocity of vehicle while Odometer is used to measure the distance traveled by the vehicle.__

questions.question: What is the change in the direction of light by a mirror called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Reflection of light

__
 
• The process through which light rays falling on the surface of an object are sent back is called a reflection of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Reflection: **The phenomena in which **light ray is sent back into the same medium** from which it is coming, on **interaction with boundary,** is called reflection.
 
• **Laws of reflection:**

 
• Angle of incidence **(θi)** = Angle of reflection **(θr)**
 
• The **incident ray, the reflected ray, and normal** to the surface of incidence always lies in the same plane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c0a9c7cdbacc21654088662dc791bc707d61d319eef7dfc8013f07612d0275f.png] 

 
• **Refraction:** When a ray of light passes from **one medium to another** it suffers a **change in direction** at the boundary of two media is called refraction.

 
• The change in direction **because the speed of light travels at different speeds **in different mediums.
 
• Refractive Index of a medium defines that it is denser or rarer
 
• **Refractive Index = Speed of light in Vacuum /speed of light in that medium.**
 
• **Refractive Index = η = c/v** where, c = Speed of light in Vacuum, v = speed of light in that medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82339a0de627554b07235929cdd32b43851718b65b7114397e275f2df207692c.png]

questions.question: Which amongst the following is NOT a noble gas?
questions.solution: The noble gases make up a group of chemical elements with similar properties, under standard conditions, they are all odorless, colorless, monatomic gases with very low chemical reactivity. The six noble gases that occur naturally are helium (He), neon (Ne), argon (Ar), krypton (Kr), xenon (Xe), and the radioactive radon (Rn).

questions.question: The autotrophs or the producers exist at which trophic level of the food chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First.**__

__Explanation:__

Feeding relation in the natural surrounding:

Food chain: 

__
 
• A food chain shows the feeding relationship between different organisms in a particular environment and/or habitat.
 
• A food chain shows how energy is passed from the sun to producers, from producers to consumers, and from consumers to decomposes such as fungi.
 
• They also show how animals depend on other organisms for food.

Tropic level: 

 
• Based on the source of their nutrition or food, organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain that is known as their trophic level.
 
• Producers belong to the first trophic level, herbivores (primary consumer) to the second and carnivores (secondary consumer) to the third. The important point to note is that the amount of energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/149da41b2e58def7608e4afb88e8bd29b90d52c1d6f0d4542f251b74e5e38052.png] 

 
• Primary producers are at first tropic level - They produce food with their own with the help of photosynthesis. Ex- plants,trees.
 
• Primary Consumers are the herbivore's animals, whose nutrition is directly based on plant products. Ex- Cow, deer, grasshoppers, small insects etc.
 
• Secondary consumers are carnivorous animals Like- small birds, wolfs etc.
 
• Tertiary Consumers are also carnivorous but they feed on secondary consumers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Only 10% of energy is transferred to higher levels from the previous one. So, the demand for food is more in higher levels. So, the food chain does not go for more than 3-4 tropic levels. This leads to more complex food forms known as a food web.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dd88533bd479397c8ff098b2f7d94cd87266b920004f4f2f9d17ef4fb30dd9b.png] 

 
• Primary (100%) → First level/ Primary (10%) → Second-level/ Secondary (1%) → Third level / Tertiary (0.1%).

questions.question: Which project allows the shipping segment from Kolkata to Sittwe in Myanmar?
questions.solution: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project is a project that will connect the eastern Indian seaport of Kolkata with Sittwe seaport in Rakhine State, Myanmar by sea. This project will reduce the distance from Kolkata to Sittwe by approximately 1328 km and will reduce the need to transport the goods through the narrow Siliguri corridor, also known as Chicken's Neck.
